subject: Post-call: decision path & procurement next steps

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + who owns budget?

Hi Liam — thanks again for the 30m earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

TL;DR: You mentioned security/procurement signoff and an econ buyer who needs to OK budget. Can you confirm names and an approximate procurement timeline so we can prepare the right artifacts?

What we covered:
- Primary use case: inference for transactional risk scoring (low-latency, high throughput)
- Target latency: 100–150ms p50 for short prompts; throughput ~2000 reqs/min initially
- Data requirements: no PII stored; logs retained 90 days

Outstanding asks from our side:
- Who is the economic buyer that signs off on budgets (name, title, best contact)?
- Who owns procurement / vendor onboarding (email for procurement team)?
- Any specific security evidence you need besides SOC 2 (e.g., pen test, iso)?

Proposed next steps:
1) Intro email to economic buyer + procurement (you can forward or I can do a short intro)
2) Deliver SOC 2 summary and 1-pager tailored to PayGrid (attached)
3) Schedule a 30-min procurement + security Q&A next week if that works

I attached a short post-call recap and 1-pager. If you prefer, I can route this to your procurement contact directly.

Best,
Dev Patel
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147
Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@paygrid.io>

Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + who owns budget?

Dev — thanks for the clear notes. Good summary.

Quick answers: Helena Morris (CFO) is ultimately the economic buyer for platform spends — she signs off on any new vendor > $50k/yr. Marcus Lee (VP, Infrastructure) will own the technical budget and implementation sign-off. Procurement at PayGrid is a shared inbox procurement@paygrid.io (procurement team triages).

Timeline: procurement + security review usually takes 2–4 weeks once we kick it off; CFO approval can add another week depending on QTR timing. For security, our minimum asks are SOC 2 Type II and an evidence summary; if you can share a short SOC 2 summary and a statement on data deletion policies that would speed review.

I can do the intro to Marcus and procurement. If you can include Helena on the loop later (email to her with contract-level numbers / ROI is usually sufficient).

Cheers,
Liam
Head of Platform Partnerships, PayGrid
liam.oconnor@paygrid.io
